The African Democratic Congress has appointed a 14-member caretaker committee to oversee its affairs in Kano State following the dissolution of the state executive committee by the party’s National Working Committee over the expiration of its tenure. The caretaker committee, which takes immediate effect, will serve for six months pending the conduct of a new election. The development was disclosed in a letter dated November 9 and signed by the party’s National Secretary, Rauf Aregbesola. A copy of the letter was made available to The PUNCH on Tuesday by the state chairman, Musa Ungogo. The committee is chaired by Alhaji Musa Ungogo, while Nura Makoda was appointed deputy chairman and Dr Bala Takai, secretary. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Other members include Tasi’u Fagge, deputy secretary; Ahmed Panda, treasurer; A’isha Kano, financial secretary; and Saidu Bello, publicity secretary. Also named are Muhammad Yahaya as legal adviser; Yusuf Bature, welfare secretary; Mamina Lamido, organising secretary; and Sa’adu Mata, auditor. Others are Adamu Mekoriya, leader of persons with disabilities; Murja Aliyu, women leader; and Isa Garo, youth leader. Amaechi compares ADC court battle to Abiola’s June 12 ordeal Kano gov unveils N50,000 grants for 5,200 women 2027: Kano gov orders LG chairmen to distribute uncollected PVCs Speaking after his appointment, Ungogo called on members of the committee to regard their positions as a responsibility to serve the party and its members. “The task ahead is clear. We must build a party that is not only a formidable political force but also a true home for every progressive-minded individual in Kano State. This committee is committed to transparency, unity, and dedicated service,” he said. He said the committee would promote inclusive leadership by accommodating diverse opinions and talents within the party. “Our elders are the bedrock of our party, and their guidance remains invaluable as we chart a new course. We will not abandon the collective wisdom that has sustained us through recent challenges,” Ungogo added. The chairman urged members across the state to close ranks and work towards building a strong grassroots movement. “Unity is not optional if we are serious about our political ambitions. Every member must put aside personal differences and focus on the larger goal of strengthening the party from the wards upward,” he stated. Ungogo also criticised the policies of the incumbent government, describing them as corrupt, divisive and unpopular. “The current administration has failed the people of Kano and Nigeria. Our duty is to organise effectively and offer the electorate a credible alternative that prioritises good governance and the welfare of ordinary citizens,” he said. Hussaini Ibrahim
